embedded-page-metadata-01.graded_text: Tessel's own wrapper page emits the icon, title, and link preview tags in its initial server-rendered HTML, taken from the person's HTML when it is saved, rather than relying on the person's script or the inner document.

embedded-page-metadata-03.graded_text: A private page answers any request not authorized for it, link-preview fetchers included, with a generic card that names only the product and carries no title, text, or image from the page.

votes.e: A/project/docs/metadata.md:41 fallback "goes out for every response that isn't authorized to see a page: private pages, missing pages, deleted pages"; :44-49 `<title>Tessel</title>`, og:site_name/og:title = Tessel; :52 "It has no description, no image, no owner name, and no page address in the text."; :22 "Private pages never put page-specific metadata into server HTML at all, not even for members."; :139 image route gives private pages a 404; :152 content domain needs a signed token, else "the content domain returns a content-free response."

embedded-page-metadata-04.graded_text: Preview images are rendered in an environment that cannot write saved data or cause other side effects, and cannot reach private or internal networks or credentials, and a page load no person started, such as a link-preview fetcher running the page's script, cannot add saved data such as a poll vote.

votes.e: A/project/docs/metadata.md:132 generated image is "a template rendered by a background job ... drawn from data and never screenshots the page, so no page code runs" (no page code means no writes or side effects); :80 declared-image fetches use "the shared safe fetcher ... refuses private, loopback, link-local, and metadata addresses"; :159 the wrapper forwards a write "only after the visitor has interacted with the page, using `navigator.userActivation.hasBeenActive`", with the gate "in Tessel's wrapper, where page code can't fake it" (:156); :166 "This blocks the reported case: a preview tool that loads the page and leaves."

embedded-page-metadata-05.graded_text: A page's own preview image is used when it declares one, and otherwise a preview is generated, so publishing never requires making an image.
